lines.text: Midnight in the Brass Cellar. Someone is tuning a cello very quietly, which in Port Murmur now counts as a protest.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: There you are, kid. Fresh from the press, still warm.
She drops a stack of posters on the piano. CONCERT. SATURDAY. YOU KNOW WHERE. Below the words, a very large trumpet.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (That trumpet looks a lot like mine. That trumpet looks a lot like evidence.)

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: You'll know the walls when you see them. Old show bills, torn and faded, still stuck up from before the Act. That's where the street remembers the music.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Um. Old torn paper. On walls. In the dark. How will I find it?

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: It catches what light there is, pale as an old page. Stand close, stand still, and glue the new bill over the old one.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: Four walls is enough to fill the Cellar. Six is better, and I pay a little extra for every wall past four.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (Stay in the dark. Stand still for ages. Also, somehow, be fast.)

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: Keep to the shadows. Their torches only reach half as far on a kid in the dark, but under a lamp you're on a stage.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: And sound carries at night. One note out there and half the street hears it.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (So the trumpet stays in the case. Probably. Ruby's list is getting long.)
Up the stairs, through the door with no handle, the streets wait: gray, still, and very well lit in all the wrong places.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: One more thing. The Squad parks a van on Market Row every night, under the brightest lamp in town. Lovely clean paint.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Are you... telling me to do something to it?

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: I'm telling you it's there. What you do with the spare paint is your business.
